simplified: For many years, I have made computer art. I create geometric art using pen and paper on plotters. I write the code for the art, and sometimes I build the machines. I would share my work on social media. I thought maybe people would like the smooth sounds and the snaps and pops. But no one really noticed it. One day, someone gave me a chocolate 3D printer extruder. I filled it with acrylic paint. I set it up and made a big mess. I wanted to try making some dots, so I wrote a small program. The dots did not come out in order. Some people reacted to this. Some were upset. Some people felt sorry for the machine. Some people danced to it. Most people were upset. The narrator said, "If you stand in a line, it will be faster. If you stand in a line, it will be quicker. I think you are moving side to side. You should stand in a line, and you will go faster. Just stand in a line!" Joshua Schachter: This story is called “Bad day at the circle factory.” I found out that you can create feelings using just a machine and some paper. So, I decided to investigate this idea. People became very upset. I got yelled at many times. It was gentle yelling. Many people said things like "I hope your pillow is warm." These stories started to get millions and millions of views. And many people had reactions too. Narrator: Circle, circle, circle, I love you. Circle, circle. Did I say my feelings too early? I said my feelings too early! It’s okay, it’s okay! JS: People wanted me to make mazes. OK. How do you mess up a maze? This is how. I went right past the exit. I had to learn the rules of this small game. It had to take 12 or maybe 15 seconds. I needed to go quickly. I also had to try to hide the fault under the mechanism. The ending had to be very sad. I promised people that it would be oddly satisfying, but then I would let them down. Many people thought this was about AI. That video became very popular. People watched my 17-second video for a total of 200,000 hours. I received so many messages that my phone died many times over several days. In the end, having limits can help create art, but you can also end up making a poor copy of your own work. I did not like that, so I decided to take a break. But remember, if you go on the internet and see something that annoys you a little, it might have been me. Thank you.
